key_insight: The detonation-sprayed FeNiCoMoW coating increased indentation hardness and reduced retained indentation depth relative to untreated AISI 321 stainless steel.
engineering_relevance: Depth-based indentation descriptors can help engineers compare coating hardness and unloading recovery without conflating retained-depth behavior with conventional contact-depth-based hardness.
method: Instrumented Vickers indentation measured maximum and residual depths in the substrate and coating.
Calculated Martens hardness HM, residual-depth-based Hpl, and their ratio.
Optical microscopy and X-ray diffraction characterized coating morphology and crystalline phases.
evidence_signal: The 145 ± 8 μm coating increased indentation hardness from 2.3 ± 0.17 to 8.65 ± 1 GPa, reduced retained-depth fraction from 0.906 to 0.788, and increased Hpl/HM from 1.22 to 1.61.
watch_item: Indentation results alone do not establish coating adhesion, wear resistance, or durability under service loading.
paper_title: Indentation Evaluation of Elastic–Plastic Response and Surface Modifications in Stainless Steel
